briefs.title: LinkedIn post: Cero asks before running mutating commands
briefs.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post for developers explaining how starting a line with '>' in Cero makes a plain-language request, and how Cero shows commands that change things for approval before running them in a real shell. Hook in the first 210 characters, 3 to 5 hashtags at the end, zero emojis, no hype words. Stick strictly to the verified facts.

briefs.title: X post: Cero local SLM and system keychain
briefs.prompt: Write a single X post (280 characters max, max 2 hashtags, zero emojis, no hype words) about Cero running its built-in local model (3B default, 2.1 GB) on your computer or using Ollama/an API of your choice with keys kept in the system keychain. Stick strictly to the verified facts.

briefs.title: Instagram caption: Cero .flow files
briefs.prompt: Write an Instagram caption (strong hook in the first 125 characters, up to 5 hashtags, zero emojis, no hype words) about Cero .flow files: one file, double-click, works on macOS/Linux/Windows, and nothing runs until you click Run. Stick strictly to the verified facts.

briefs.title: Blog intro paragraph: Why Cero previews commands in a real shell
briefs.prompt: Write an opening intro paragraph (120 to 180 words, direct builder-to-builder tone, zero emojis, no hype words) for an engineering blog post about how Cero works in a real shell (zsh/bash, PowerShell on Windows), asks before running state-changing commands, and answers from real output. Stick strictly to the verified facts.

briefs.title: Community reply: Does Cero run commands without asking?
briefs.prompt: Write a short, direct developer community reply (280 characters max, zero emojis, no hype words) answering the question: 'Does Cero run commands without asking?' Base every claim strictly on the verified facts.
